ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$, where point A corresponds to point D, and point B corresponds to point E. If $\angle A=70^\circ$ and $\angle B=50^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle 1$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=70^\circ$, $\angle B=50^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle C=180^\circ-\angle A-\angle B=180^\circ-70^\circ-50^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
since $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$,\\
it follows that $\angle 1=\angle C=\boxed{60^\circ}$
